action.message: NCCP recommends 50% of the original axitinib dose in Child-Pugh B; EMA gives 5 mg twice daily to 2 mg twice daily as an example. Reconcile the prescribed tablet dose with pharmacy; do not automatically prescribe 2.5 mg twice daily.

action.message: Avoid strong CYP3A4/5 inhibitors where possible. If unavoidable, NCCP recommends approximately halving the dose (example 5→2 mg twice daily). Confirm interaction and reversal plans; do not stack reductions automatically.

action.message: Avoid strong CYP3A4/5 inducers where possible. Any gradual dose increase needs specialist monitoring; if the inducer stops, return promptly to the pre-inducer dose according to the source.

action.message: Escalation is a prescribing decision: source criteria require two consecutive weeks without toxicity above grade 2, BP no higher than 150/90 and no antihypertensive treatment. Steps are 5→7→10 mg twice daily; an isolated acceptable BP or absent input does not establish eligibility.

rules.explanation: Escalation is a prescribing decision: source criteria require two consecutive weeks without toxicity above grade 2, BP no higher than 150/90 and no antihypertensive treatment. Steps are 5→7→10 mg twice daily; an isolated acceptable BP or absent input does not establish eligibility.

eligibility: Advanced clear-cell renal cell carcinoma after prior sunitinib or a cytokine
Adequate organ and haematological function; source exclusions and prior-treatment criteria must be checked.
exclusions: Known hypersensitivity to a regimen component
Pregnancy or breastfeeding where prohibited by the current source
Regimen-specific exclusions encoded in the assessment

supportive_care.mapping_basis: Current source-specific support plan; verify local prescription.
supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for oral SACT
premedication: No routine infusion premedication is required. The team prescribes any sickness medicine under local policy.
other_support: Collect a prescription for diarrhoea medicine, usually loperamide, before starting. Follow the supplied instructions and contact the team for persistent diarrhoea, dizziness, poor intake or reduced urine.

treatment_phases.name: Continuous oral treatment

administration.notes: Approximately 12 hours apart, with or without food; no fixed course length.

treatment_phases.label: 5 mg twice daily continuously; no planned rest week
treatment_phases.summary: Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity, with individual prescribing review.

baseline: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests, thyroid tests, urine protein and blood-pressure assessment. Review heart and vascular history, current medicines and recent surgery.
regular: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests regularly; thyroid tests every four weeks. Blood pressure weekly during the first cycle, then every four weeks; urine protein every three months.
monitoring.disease_monitoring: Symptoms and scans are interpreted together. Your consultant sets imaging timing according to the treatment plan; this regimen does not mandate a universal three-month scan interval.
